title: AssessmentRequest

AssessmentOptions.description: How far to run and over which engines. Echoed in the result as applied.

target_engines.description: Engine scope: the engine catalog ids to consider. None means every engine the workload warrants. Ids are lower-cased, trimmed, de-duplicated and sorted; an empty list, a legacy id, a planned engine or an unknown id is refused.
target_engines.title: Target Engines

run_through.description: Last phase to run. 'analysis' scores every statement and assigns nothing; 'reality_check' adds the final engine placement; 'schema_design' designs the data model of every engine the placement keeps; 'synthesis' adds the report. 'schema_design' and 'synthesis' need a model (deterministic=False); their designs and report are in `artifacts`.
run_through.title: Run Through

deterministic.description: Run with no model. Analysis never uses one; with False the reality check has a model review its consolidations and write its summary, schema design designs with a model and synthesis writes its executive summary with one. Must be False for 'schema_design' and 'synthesis'.
deterministic.title: Deterministic

include_artifacts.description: Include the internal contracts in `artifacts` (no compatibility promise).
include_artifacts.title: Include Artifacts

AssessmentOptions.title: AssessmentOptions

UnplacedStatement.description:
A statement a cut could not place: it reads no table of the collection, so it
belongs to no cut's tables.

reason.description: no_tables_read: it reads no table (a procedure call, a sequence read, a function call, a session command); tables_not_collected: it reads only tables the collection does not hold (system catalogs, an unlisted materialized view)
reason.title: Reason

UnplacedStatement.title: UnplacedStatement

WorkloadScope.description:
Informational: what a cut workload left out. Echoed back unchanged; no rule reads it.

``cut_collection`` (#1633) writes one for each cut: the tables kept, the statement
parts in ``rewritten_query_ids``, the foreign keys it cut in ``dropped_foreign_keys``
and the statements it could not place in ``unplaced_statements``.

rewritten_query_ids.description: Statements the caller rewrote; marked rewritten_by_caller in the result.
rewritten_query_ids.title: Rewritten Query Ids

dropped_foreign_keys.description: Foreign keys the cut workload left out. cut_collection writes one object per foreign key between a kept table and a dropped one: constraint_name, table_id (the table that holds the key) and referenced_table_id. Any other object is echoed as given
dropped_foreign_keys.title: Dropped Foreign Keys

unplaced_statements.description: The statements the cut left out because they read no table of the collection (none of them belongs to any cut's tables), each with its reason, unless the caller gave a part for it
unplaced_statements.title: Unplaced Statements

WorkloadScope.title: WorkloadScope

description: One assessment: a database's raw collection and the options to run it with.

contract_version.description: The contract version the caller builds on: 1.3 or 1.4; the result is written for it. With none, the newest version a release recorded (src/assessment/released_contract.json, written after the release's tag, so the release that first ships a version still defaults to the one before): a newer version is read only when pinned. A 1.3 request cannot set a field 1.4 added (routine_sources). The retired 1.0, 1.1 and 1.2 are refused with RetiredContractVersionError; any other value is refused as invalid
contract_version.title: Contract Version

database_name.description: 1 to 128 ASCII letters, digits, underscores or hyphens, not starting with a hyphen.
database_name.title: Database Name

collection.description: A raw collection: the unmodified output of the collection scripts (statement text, execution statistics and the schema), or a cut's collection (cut_collection). A collector output (any version the library reads) is accepted too, but every derived fact is read again from each statement's text by the library's parser; derived fields it carries are ignored.
collection.title: Collection

routine_sources.description: Contract 1.4 (pin contract_version 1.4): each routine's CREATE statement, in the routine-sources format: RoutineSource entries (kind, routine_id, schema_name, specific_name, create_statement, origin, and optionally exact, inexact_reason, session, sha256; an unknown key is refused; docs/contracts/assess.md, Routine sources). A 1.4 run writes the job's routine sources, its index and chunks, as the collection scripts and live collectors do, and nowhere else: never in the result. An entry is used for its routine as given; every other routine a raw collection holds a body for is extracted from it as the scripts extract it. Only a PostgreSQL, MySQL or MariaDB routine the collection lists with its body collected gets one, an entry is written exact only when the collection does not mark the routine's body not exact, an origin of another engine is refused, and a collection made with include_routine_bodies = 0 gets none. None (the default) and [] give no entry. Two entries for one routine (kind, schema_name, specific_name) are refused. The request never serializes this field
routine_sources.title: Routine Sources
